title: The Story of the Year
summary: The sparrows sat shivering in the bare branches, chirping: "When will spring return? Winter is so long and cruel!"...
full_text:
The sparrows sat shivering in the bare branches, chirping: "When will spring return? Winter is so long and cruel!"

Old King Winter sat on his throne of snow, blowing icy gales across the forest. But beneath the frozen crust, the Earth Mother was awakening.

Suddenly, two storks flew across the sky, bearing young Spring on their wings. Warm sunbeams melted the snow, larks sang in the blue vault, and green leaves burst from the dormant trees.

Spring matured into golden Summer with heavy wheat sheaves; Summer ripened into mellow Autumn with purple grapes; and Autumn surrendered to King Winter once more.

The sparrows chirped: "The year is dead!" But the wise old raven cawed: "The year never dies; it only turns its circle, and in the coldest frost, the promise of new life is already born."
moral: The seasons of life change in relentless rhythm, yet every winter conceals the seeds of spring.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Story of the Year"?
options: Andersen's tales teach compassion, resilience, and Christian hope
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
